clue.text: Cautious about Italian making donation

indicators.note: about means the word for cautious goes around the abbreviation for Italian

parts.note: chary means cautious or wary
IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian (as in gin and it)

explanation.surface: A wary Italian makes a gift to a good cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity can mean a gift given to those in need, a synonym of donation.

clue.text: Principal part of building where nuts should fit in?

parts.note: head means chief or principal, as in head teacher
a room is one part of a building

explanation.surface: A main room is where some nuts belong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' is slang for heads, so headroom is where heads fit under a ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the clear space above your head; nut is slang for the head, so it is where a nut fits.

clue.text: Artist wearing plaster that protects from cats and dogs

definitions.text: that protects from cats and dogs

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
wearing means in, as in dressed in a suit
a coat of plaster is a layer spread on a wall

explanation.surface: A painter in a plaster cast protects against feline and canine pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cats and dogs' is not about pets: it is rain, from the idiom raining cats and dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat worn to keep off rain shields you in a downpour, which the idiom describes as raining cats and dogs.

clue.text: Established supporting vehicles one should leave immobile

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the word for established sits beneath, after the vehicles
should leave means the numeral for one goes out of the vehicles word

parts.note: trains are vehicles on rails
I is the Roman numeral for one
fixed means established or settled

explanation.surface: Something set up on top of vehicles must stay still.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking I from TRAINS leaves TRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Transfixed means held motionless, as with shock or wonder.

clue.text: Gold must come next to be dandy

indicators.note: must come next to places the gold symbol beside the little word be, after it

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Gold must follow for things to be fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a fashionable man who cares about his clothes, which is what a dandy is.

clue.text: Kind of economic policy in the red, turning green?

parts.note: a red traffic light tells you to stop
when the light turns green you may go

explanation.surface: An economic policy for a country in debt that is going environmental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' sounds like debt and 'green' like the environment; both are traffic lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop-go is a British economic policy of alternately restraining and stimulating demand.

clue.text: Militant cardinal mixed up, losing direction

indicators.note: a mixed-up word has its letters jumbled
losing means a compass letter is dropped from the churchman's word

parts.note: N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A confused church leader turns militant after losing his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes N from CARDINAL to leave CARDIAL, which 'mixed up' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical is an extremist or militant who wants sweeping change.

clue.text: Playgoer ignoring unknown performing show of bloomers to be put on here

definitions.text: show of bloomers to be put on here

indicators.note: performing means the theatre-goer's letters act out a new arrangement
ignoring means a letter for an unknown is left out of the theatre-goer word

parts.note: Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer ignores a stranger on stage putting on a show of bloomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' takes Y from PLAYGOER to leave PLAGOER, which 'performing' rearranges. 'bloomers' are flowers, not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is a garden frame over which climbing flowering plants are trained for display.

clue.text: Damaged cassette leads to legal action

indicators.note: a damaged tape is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken tape prompts someone to sue.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose verdict sets a precedent for others, so it is a kind of legal action.

clue.text: Dress at home

parts.note: a habit is a dress or garment, as worn by a nun or a rider

explanation.surface: Someone is getting dressed while at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or surroundings of an animal or plant.

clue.text: Heather's put by tip for something to eat

indicators.note: put by means the plant word is placed beside the word for a rubbish tip, after it

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
ling is a name for the heather plant

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather has left something next to the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name but is the plant, ling. A tip in Britain is a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumpling is a ball of dough cooked in a stew, so it is a vague but fair food description.

clue.text: Place of fantasy — fear grips chap getting left inside

indicators.note: grips means the word for fear holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: dread is fear

indicators.note: getting left inside means the letter for left goes within the chap word

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Fear has a man in its grip as he goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is an imaginary world of dreams, a realm of fantasy.

clue.text: Broken carafes European's dropped in commotion …

indicators.note: broken carafes are shattered, so their letters are rearranged
dropped means the letter for European is removed from the bottles' letters

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Smashed wine jugs, dropped by a European, cause a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes E from CARAFES to leave CARAFS, which 'Broken' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or brawl, the same as a commotion.

clue.text: … 12 that shouldn't cost anybody anything

definitions.meaning: the answer to 12, a commotion or brawl, means a chaotic fight open to everyone
read literally, something given at no charge to everyone

explanation.surface: Continuing from 12, the commotion is something nobody pays for.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 12, so the first definition is that answer, FRACAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl joined by everyone is a common idiom for a fracas; read literally, the words also mean costing nobody anything.

clue.text: Pop festival in June

parts.note: a pop festival sounds like a music event, but Pop is a word for a dad, and his special day falls in June

explanation.surface: A summer music festival held in June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests pop music; it means dad.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain and the US the day honouring dads is the third Sunday in June.

clue.text: Medic returns a harmonious conclusion?

indicators.note: returns means the word for medic is read backwards

parts.note: a doc is a doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A doctor comes back with a happy ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a piece of music, hence a conclusion in harmony.

clue.text: It shows the cost of getting taken for a ride

definitions.text: It shows the cost of getting taken for a ride

parts.words: It shows the cost of getting taken for a ride
parts.note: being taken for a ride sounds like being cheated, but here it is a literal ride in a cab whose fare is displayed by a meter

explanation.surface: Something reveals how much it costs to be conned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken for a ride' usually means swindled; here it is literal, a passenger in a cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A taximeter is the device in a cab that displays the fare for the journey.

clue.text: Disorganised choirmaster missing most of mass in oratory

indicators.note: disorganised letters are put out of order
missing means the trimmed church-service letters are taken out of the choir leader word
most of means the word mass loses its last letter

parts.note: mass is written as it stands, a church service

explanation.surface: A chaotic choir leader skips much of the service in a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts MASS to MAS; 'missing' takes that from CHOIRMASTER to leave CHOIRTER, which 'Disorganised' rearranges. 'oratory' could be a chapel but means speechmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive public speaking, which is oratory.

clue.text: Mix company drinks before City rises

indicators.note: before means the beers come ahead of the City piece

parts.note: ales are drinks of beer

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: EC, East Central, is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A firm's drinks come before the City goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to come together and merge, which is to mix.

clue.text: Diplomat gets cheers rising and falling — revolutionary

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for thanks is read upwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
the same ta, this time read downwards
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: An envoy hears cheers going up and down, then a rebel appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' gives TA twice: once 'rising' (AT) and once 'falling', read normally down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is an embassy official with a specialist role, a junior member of diplomatic staff.

clue.text: Stop before opening

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: Halt before the doors open.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it happening.

clue.text: What Santa repeatedly says reverted to shout of derision

parts.note: Father Christmas laughs ho ho ho, saying ho over and over

indicators.note: reverted means the little word to is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Santa's familiar laugh turns into jeering.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoot is a jeer or scornful cry, as in hoots of derision from a crowd.

clue.text: Scruffy bit of publicity, taking shifty breather outside

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters go around the advertisement word
shifty letters move about, so the word breather is rearranged

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a bit of publicity

explanation.surface: A shabby advertisement features a dodgy pause for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifty' is the anagram signal and 'taking ... outside' means the jumbled breath word wraps round the advert; 'Scruffy' at the front is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare means worn thin and shabby, as scruffy clothing is.

clue.text: A loose woman in the family

parts.note: to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A promiscuous woman in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: An auntie is a parent's sister, a female relative.

clue.text: Renegade let out shaking noise

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or turncoat, a renegade

indicators.note: out signals the word let is put out of order

explanation.surface: A traitor is set free.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattle is a rapid clattering sound, the noise something makes when shaken.

clue.text: Progressed, getting offered money?

definitions.meaning: being lent cash ahead of time, as with a loan on wages

explanation.surface: Someone moved up in life after being given cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced means moved forward, and money advanced is a sum paid out early or lent.

clue.text: Partially consumed a mild cheese

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has eaten part of a gentle-tasting cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coating, an example of the category.

clue.text: Speech could be flat

definitions.meaning: a formal talk given to an audience
a flat or home is where someone lives, identified by street and number

explanation.surface: A talk might be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an adjective (a dull speech) but is a noun for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech, and also the location of a residence such as a flat.

clue.text: Hindrance of course

definitions.meaning: belonging to a racecourse or golf course, where extra weight or strokes even out competitors

explanation.surface: Naturally, something holds you back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means a racecourse or golf course, where a horse carries extra weight or a golfer receives strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is any disadvantage, and in golf or horse racing a penalty or allowance used to equalise contestants.

clue.text: Caught New York student heading west — he had knocked off illegally

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means the pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a learner driver
he'd is the contraction of he had, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A New York student was caught going west after a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' reverses C, NY and L to give LYNC. L-plates mark British learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lynched is to be killed by a mob without legal trial, murdered outside the law.
